compute: GPU 3, fold-4 pilot ~1 h (frozen encoder forward over 7150 rows x 3 epochs, head only)
question: Backlog item 1: does a density/count head with strong point supervision (20 images) and weak CD-integral supervision (all training rows, uniform-density assumption) produce a CD estimate that is complementary to recipe A?
prior: p0: frame-level counts from the detectors are uninformative because the detectors fire only on an ROI-like cluster; the density head is trained to integrate to CD x frame area, so it must spread density over the frame. The hidden ROI makes the weak label noisy (frame-mean vs ROI density).

design.head: Linear 768->1 + softplus on frozen fold-4 recipe A tokens (encoder never updated)
design.strong: per-patch L1 to the normalised Gaussian count density inside the ROI + integral error, 20 train-green x 4 flips
design.weak: |log(frame integral / 0.7528 mm^2) - log CD| on all 7150 fold-4 training rows
design.training: 3 epochs, batch 4 (+1 strong item per step), AdamW 1e-3, seed 46

evaluation: fold-4 validation rows (leaked rows excluded): r(log CD_density, log GT CD), error correlation with the adopted prediction, MAPE after one median scale; point F1 of density peaks on the 5 validation-green images (information)
pre_specified_decision: extend to five folds and a LOFO blend only if error correlation <= 0.6 and one-scale MAPE <= 9% (the blend arithmetic needed for a 0.03 pp gain); otherwise close backlog item 1 as negative with these numbers
falsification: error correlation >= 0.7 (like the spacing estimator) means the weak integral label just reproduces the regressor's errors.
